scope: Splendor core game, 1st edition (2014), complete authoritative extracted/splendor-rules.txt. No expansions or later-edition additions.

questions.question: Set up a two-player game. How many tokens of each gem color and how many gold tokens remain, how many nobles are revealed, and what happens to unrevealed nobles?
For three players, give the gem-token count per color, gold-token count and noble count. How do those counts differ in a four-player game?
Describe how the development decks and market are prepared: shuffling, order of the three levels, and face-up card counts. Who starts and in which direction does play proceed?
List all four action choices on a turn. May you take gems and then buy a card on the same turn, or reserve and buy that reserved card on that same turn?
What information about tokens you own must be visible to other players, and when?

A green pile contains four tokens; a red pile contains three. Can you take two green, leaving two? Can you take two red? When is the supply threshold checked, and can either gem-taking action take gold?
You begin with nine tokens and take three different gems. Is temporarily holding twelve allowed, how many must you return, can they include the gems just drawn, and does gold count toward the limit?
You have ten tokens and fewer than three reserved cards. You reserve a card while gold is available. What happens to the gold and your token count, and what if the gold supply were empty instead?
From which two places may you reserve a card? If reserving from a deck, which card is taken and is it shown to opponents? Who may eventually buy a reserved card?

You already have three reserved cards and want a fourth, or just want the gold from reserving. Can you reserve now? May you discard or exchange a reserved card to make room, and how can a reserved card leave your hand?

You reserve a face-up level-2 card while that deck has cards left. When and from where is the empty market space refilled? How does this differ when purchasing a face-up card, buying a reserved card, or when the relevant deck is empty?
A card costs two blue and one green. You have two blue bonuses and no green bonus. What tokens must you spend? What if your bonuses cover every required color, and are bonuses spent when used?

A card costs three blue, two black and one white. You have two blue bonuses, one black bonus, and no white bonus; your available payment is one blue token and two gold. Can you buy it? State which costs the tokens cover, where all spent tokens go, and whether your bonus cards stay with you.
Which cards can you purchase with a buy action? After purchase, how should acquired development cards be arranged, and which information on them must always remain visible?

A noble requires three blue, three green and three white bonuses. You have three blue cards, three green cards, two white cards and a white token (or a gold token). Do you qualify? What changes if you instead acquire a third white bonus, and do bonuses above a requirement disqualify you?

At the end of your action you qualify for two nobles. Can you take both, decline all visits, or choose one? Does the visit use another action, how many points does it give, and when is eligibility checked?
Once you receive a noble, where is its tile placed, and is it face up or hidden?

In a four-player game, turns run A, B, C, D, with A first. B reaches fifteen prestige points on their turn. Who still takes a turn before the game ends, does A take another turn, and is B guaranteed to win?

You have thirteen prestige points and receive a noble at the end of your turn. What is your new total, does that trigger the end of the game even though you skipped over fifteen, and when is the winner determined?

At the end, A has sixteen prestige and ten purchased developments; B has sixteen prestige and nine purchased developments plus three cards still reserved; C has fifteen prestige and only five purchased developments. Who wins and why? Do nobles count toward prestige, and do B’s reserved cards count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker?
